text.p: Suez Cement made net attributable profits of 190 million pounds ($56 million) in the first nine months of 1996, against 280 million in all of 1995, the state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories said on Friday.
The company's cement production in the whole of 1996 was 2.879 million tonnes, against 2.867 tonnes in 1995, it said.
Net revenue from operations was 365 million pounds in the nine-month period, compared with 466 million in all 1995.

The holding company, which retains a stake in Suez Cement, said work was under way on a second line at the company's Suez plant to produce 1.35 million tonnes a year and on expanding the first production line by 215,000 tonnes a year.
These projects will increase the company's capacity to 4.3 million tonnes a year, it said. It did not say when the extra capacity would come on stream.

The nine-month profits are equivalent to 3.88 pounds for each of the 49 million shares. The shares closed on the Egyptian stock exchange on Thursday at 72.03 pounds. The Suez Cement GDR was quoted at $19.85/20.25, a discount on the Cairo price.
